title: Salt and Wolf
premise: Vesper Nakamura, exiled for a storm she cannot remember calling, has spent seven years hiding her gift behind guild ledgers that record trades in impossible things. When the crown's witch-hunt reaches the port city of Greyharbor, she discovers the king himself is bound to an ancient entity wearing his crown — and that her forgotten storm was the first attempt to stop it. To unbind him, Vesper must recover her stolen memories from the entity itself, ally with the hunt's disillusioned captain, and choose between restoring her own past and saving a kingdom that exiled her. In the end she breaks the binding by taking the crown's burden into herself, then walks into the sea to scatter it, remembered by no one but the ledger.
about_author: F. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing salvaged ship logs off the West African coast before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things the world would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She audits a trade of bottled thunder at the Saltglass Guild, hiding her storm-caller's gift behind clerical calm. A client pays with a coin minted by a dead king — still warm. The beat is quiet dread: her careful, recordable life is starting to smell like lightning.

chapters.title: Proclamation
chapters.summary: Captain Ivo Renner's POV. He reads the crown's edict: all gifted persons to be seized for 'examination.' His orders include a sealed list of names — his own sister among them. The beat is moral fracture: a lawman realizing the law has turned predatory.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hunters raid the Guild; Vesper's suppressed gift flares, leveling the street, and she flees with only the ledgers. An old woman shelters her and calls her by a name Vesper doesn't remember choosing. The beat is terror giving way to vertigo: her exile has holes in it.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Summoned to the capital, he witnesses the king give an order in two voices — one human, one vast and patient beneath it. Ivo pockets the name-list instead of executing it. The beat is horrified recognition: the hunt is the entity feeding.

chapters.title: The Storm She Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following ledger clues to a drowned village, she finds survivors who remember her standing in the surf seven years ago, calling down lightning at the royal procession — and then nothing. The beat is grief: the person she was tried to save everyone and paid in memory.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ivo tracks Vesper intending arrest; instead they trade truths over a fire — his sister, her erased night — and strike a bargain: he gets her inside the palace, she proves the king is bound. The beat is wary trust between two people trained to betray.

chapters.title: The Examination Halls
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, disguised as a captured gifted woman. In the palace cells she finds the 'examinations' are harvests — the entity drinking memory and power. She finds the old woman from Chapter 3, emptied and smiling. The beat is cold fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Audience
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He presents Vesper as his prisoner to buy audience with the king. Alone, the king briefly surfaces and begs Ivo to end it — then the entity speaks through him, offering Vesper her memories back in exchange for the ledgers. The beat is temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the throne room she refuses the trade and begins the unbinding rite written in her own lost handwriting in the ledgers' margins. Ivo holds the guards; the entity tears her memories open as payment. The beat is sacrificial climax: she chooses the kingdom's future over her own past.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, fragmented then clear. Binding the entity means carrying it, so she writes one final entry — names, debts, truth — and walks into the Greyharbor tide as the storm finally breaks clean. Ivo burns the hunt's list. The beat is bittersweet release: justice outside the law, remembered only in ink.
